headline: Europe and Asia rebound on a US tariff-cap pledge while Wall Street shuts for Thanksgiving
subhead: The DAX recovered to 25,215.5 and Brazil's Bovespa jumped 6.1% on Thursday, after Wednesday's 0.3% S&P 500 slip and Nvidia's 3.9% fall on an S&P CreditWatch.

us.text: The S&P 500 slipped 0.3% to 7,182.8 and the Nasdaq 0.6% on Wednesday after erasing most of a 3.2% intraday drop; markets shut Thursday.
October core PCE rose 3.3%, above forecasts, cementing bets on a December Fed hike; the 10-year yield fell 1.1% to 4.85%.
Nvidia fell 3.9% after S&P put its AA rating on CreditWatch negative; Oracle lost 5.1% and Meta gained 3.4%. Friday's session ends at 1 pm ET.

india.text: The Nifty jumped 1.9% to 25,819.3 on 25 Nov as FMCG and banks led, then extended gains to 25,884.5 on 26 Nov.
FIIs net bought Rs 5,843 crore on 26 Nov, an 18th straight session of buying, after Rs 4,479 crore on 25 Nov.
The rupee settled 24 paise weaker at 92.44 per dollar on 26 Nov as crude rose toward 95 dollars and US tariff fears returned.

global.text: Asian shares rebounded on 26 Nov led by AI stocks, after the Taiex fell 4.8% and the Hang Seng 1.1% on 25 Nov.
European stocks rallied on 26 Nov, the DAX rising to 25,215.5, after the US said it would cap new duties at levels agreed in trade deals.
Brazil's Bovespa jumped 6.1% to 176,800, its second-best day of 2026, on Finance Ministry speculation; bitcoin held near 60,600 dollars.

weekly.narrative: An AI unwind dominated the week: Anthropic's record Nasdaq debut failed to steady sentiment, Nvidia fell 22.9 percent and the Nasdaq 10.0 percent, its worst week since March 2020, while the S&P 500 lost 8.6 percent and closed in correction. Near-certain bets on a December Fed hike pushed gold down 8.1 percent and silver 14.4 percent to near 52-week lows, and bitcoin fell 5.8 percent toward its 2026 low. India stood apart as heavy foreign buying lifted the Nifty to a nine-month high of 25,800.6 and Bank Nifty to records, while Tokyo, Seoul and Frankfurt followed Wall Street lower. Next week is shortened by Thanksgiving and turns on US PCE inflation and GDP on 25 November, ahead of the Fed decision on 9 December.
